I do a lot of shopping at DressBarn (or Roz & Ali depending on if your location was bought recently). For the most part the fits are very true to size and I've recently done a lot of online ordering and everything was exactly how it appeared, in the exact size. If you sign up for emails they send coupons and I usually only buy on sale or clearance. I got 5 dresses last week that were originally $70 each for $70 total. And they are good quality too, they will hold up for years, but will require dry cleaning.

Kohl's is decent, and they always have coupons, but you'll have to dig through clearance racks. I've found great things there though, but not with the designer collections. The designer material is usually thin and will tear or wash out of shape easily.

Finally, depending on where you live, Stein-Mart is inexpensive, they offer lots of coupons and clearances, and everything is very high quality. Women's clothes there do lean to the conservative side because most is professional wear, and their dresses are gorgeous. Same with shoes. Everything holds up to wash and wear very well. Plus, a large part of what you spend goes back to the community through charity, which I appreciate.
